observationsNotFindings.where: remeasurementClause, 'does not unwrite D-086, D-117, D-167 through D-332'
observationsNotFindings.observation: The predecessor carried this clause as 'D-167 through D-283', and the accepted Claude review of that version licensed the range by verifying contiguity: 117 distinct headings for a range of 117, 'so the remeasurement clause's D-167 through D-283 names only live headings'. That licence has lapsed at v5. D-167 through D-332 spans 166 numbers but only 165 live headings; D-319 was drafted and reviewed but never recorded, and twelve coordinator-decisions.D-319.* artifacts sit on disk with no '## D-319' heading in COORD. The subject is the only artifact in the register using a D-167-through range that crosses D-319; the sibling lineages moved to explicit enumerations instead (sdk leftover-join.v9: 'does not unwrite D-086, D-145, D-184, D-217, D-267, D-298, D-323, D-327, or D-328').
observationsNotFindings.whyNotAFinding: The clause is a denial, not an enumeration of recordings: it asserts what the speaker does not do, and it is true - the speaker unwrites nothing, D-319 included, vacuously. The one reading under which it would imply a recording is foreclosed two fields later by doesNot, which the author ADDED at this version precisely because the range now crosses the gap: 'Does not invent D-319 as a recorded heading.' and 'Does not overwrite D-319 drafts.' That pair is byte-identical to the pair carried by frozen sdk leftover-join.v9, recorded at D-329 under dual ACCEPT 0/0 with the same live gap. So the guard is the sanctioned one and its presence is evidence the gap was noticed rather than missed. Nothing recorded would be false and no dispatch attack succeeds through it. A later successor would nonetheless be safer enumerating headings the way the g20 and sdk lineages now do, since the range wording will keep crossing the gap and each future reviewer has to re-derive the same conclusion.

observationsNotFindings.observation: The obligation moved into summary.specifiedNotLeftover while keeping the predecessor's rideStanding 'not-capable-of-riding as execution-only remainder'. Its bucket-mate OBL-G19-NAMED-CATALOG carries rideStanding 'specified-not-leftover', so within this one file the two members of the same bucket disagree about which standing puts them there - the shape that normally signals an incomplete sweep.

Every leftover-join that has flipped an FX-AUTHORING obligation false while its gate lineage still holds the remainder carries exactly this combination: g20 leftover-join.v12, v13, v14, v15 and v16, and sdk leftover-join.v8 and v9. Two of those are current recorded remasurements taken at dual ACCEPT 0/0 within the last three days (sdk v9 at D-329, g20 v16 at D-330). The rideStanding describes why the obligation cannot ride a gate - it is an execution-only remainder - while the summary bucket describes where the leftover measurement lands; they answer different questions and the register consistently lets them differ.

observationsNotFindings.whyNotAFinding: Occupancy v2 is frozen at D-222 and its DR-124 roster is explicitly sourced to state-class leftover-join.v3 (D-183) in its own leftoverDesignRemainingOnDR124Note; it predates D-299, D-331 and D-332, which are the three recordings that make the fourth member stale. The subject nowhere claims occupancy v2 supports the three-member roster - it cites occupancy v2 for exactly three things, the leftoverDesignAlreadyClosed membership of OBL-G19-HARNESS-SPEC, the empty leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded, and the platform list, and all three are verbatim true. Charging this would amount to requiring a frozen predecessor to have anticipated later recordings.

observationsNotFindings.observation: The subject names g19 leftover-join.v4 and g19 leftover-join.v6 as not-current but omits g19 leftover-join.v7, which D-332 also freezes with the instruction 'Frozen g19 leftover-join.v7 stays frozen; do not record it as current'.
observationsNotFindings.whyNotAFinding: The selection is principled rather than partial: v4 (D-256) and v6 (D-322) are the only g19 joins ever recorded as current, whereas v7 was REJECTed at Stage A on both sides and was never current, so there is no currency claim for the subject to deny. The sanctioned sibling template is in any case more conservative than the subject here - sdk leftover-join.v9 names no g20 join version at all in its 'as current' denials, confining them to its own lineage plus occupancy v1. Both named identifiers exist on disk with live recordings, so nothing is invented.
